# datespan

**Headless, accessible, zero-dependency React date picker and month range picker.** About 3 kB per picker.

```bash
npm i datespan
```

- **Month range picker as a first-class feature:** "From"/"To" month grids, a one-grid stepped mode for mobile, presets ("Last 12 months", "2024") and a draft → Select/Cancel flow. `onChange` gives `{ start, end, from: '2025-03', to: '2025-06', preset }`, with `end` = last millisecond of the last month.
- **A conventional date picker:** a day grid that zooms out to months and years, a text input that parses typing, and min/max/disabled dates.
- **Headless:** unstyled compound components for speed, and hooks with prop getters for full control. You style it with `data-*` attributes.
- **Accessible:** the WAI-ARIA grid pattern with full keyboard support, RTL support and focus management. Checked by axe in jsdom and in Chromium.
- **No date library:** timezone-free calendar math (tested in 6 timezones), localized through the built-in `Intl` API.

<!-- sizes -->
| Import (minified + brotli, React excluded) | Size |
| --- | --- |
| useMonthRangePicker + presets | 2.76 kB |
| useDatePicker | 2.86 kB |
| usePopover | 0.74 kB |
| everything | 5.27 kB |
<!-- /sizes -->

## Month range picker

This is a reporting-period picker: presets plus From/To grids in a popover. On desktop the user confirms with **Select**. On mobile there's one grid: pick the first month, then the last.

<!-- example: time-period -->
```tsx
import { calendarYear, type DateRange, lastNMonths, MonthRangePicker, usePopover } from 'datespan'
import { useState, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react'

const MOBILE = '(max-width: 640px)'
const useMobile = () =>
  useSyncExternalStore(
    (cb) => (matchMedia(MOBILE).addEventListener('change', cb), () => matchMedia(MOBILE).removeEventListener('change', cb)),
    () => matchMedia(MOBILE).matches,
  )

/** Reporting period: presets + From/To month grids in a popover. Desktop confirms with Apply; mobile picks in two steps. */
export function TimePeriod() {
  const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange>(() => lastNMonths(12).range(new Date()))
  const pop = usePopover()
  const mobile = useMobile()

  return (
    <MonthRangePicker.Root
      value={range}
      onChange={(v) => {
        if (v) setRange(v)
        pop.close()
      }}
      open={pop.isOpen} // closing without Apply discards the draft
      presets={[lastNMonths(12), calendarYear(-1, { label: 'Last year' })]}
      max={new Date()}
      layout={mobile ? 'stepped' : 'dual'}
      commit={mobile ? 'instant' : 'confirm'}
    >
      {(picker) => (
        <>
          <button {...pop.getTriggerProps({ 'aria-label': `Time period: ${picker.label}` })}>{picker.label}</button>
          {pop.isOpen && (
            <div {...pop.getPopoverProps({ 'aria-label': 'Time period', className: 'popup' })}>
              {picker.step === 'from' && <MonthRangePicker.Presets aria-label="Presets" />}
              <MonthRangePicker.Grids />
              {!mobile && (
                <footer>
                  <MonthRangePicker.Cancel onClick={pop.close}>Cancel</MonthRangePicker.Cancel>
                  <MonthRangePicker.Apply>Apply</MonthRangePicker.Apply>
                </footer>
              )}
            </div>
          )}
          {/* ISO months for your API, e.g. "2024-11 → 2025-10" */}
          <output>{picker.value && `${picker.value.from} → ${picker.value.to}`}</output>
        </>
      )}
    </MonthRangePicker.Root>
  )
}
```
<!-- /example -->

## Date picker

<!-- example: date-field -->
```tsx
import { DatePicker, usePopover } from 'datespan'
import { useId, useState } from 'react'

/** Date input that parses typing, plus a calendar popover. */
export function DateField() {
  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | null>(null)
  const pop = usePopover()
  const errorId = useId()

  return (
    <DatePicker.Root
      value={date}
      onChange={(d) => {
        setDate(d) // also fires when typed text is committed (blur / Enter)
        pop.close() // no-op when the calendar isn't open
      }}
      format="dd/MM/yyyy"
      max={new Date()}
    >
      {(picker) => (
        <>
          <DatePicker.Input aria-label="Date of birth" aria-describedby={errorId} />
          <button {...pop.getTriggerProps({ 'aria-label': 'Open calendar' })}>📅</button>
          {pop.isOpen && (
            <div {...pop.getPopoverProps({ 'aria-label': 'Choose date', className: 'popup' })}>
              <DatePicker.Calendar />
            </div>
          )}
          <p id={errorId} role="status">
            {picker.isInputInvalid && 'Enter a past date as dd/mm/yyyy'}
          </p>
        </>
      )}
    </DatePicker.Root>
  )
}
```
<!-- /example -->

## Full control with hooks

The compound components are thin wrappers. When you need your own markup, use the hooks. Both return the same shape: `title`, `rows` of cells, and prop getters you spread on your elements.

<!-- example: month-range-hook -->
```tsx
import { lastNMonths, useMonthRangePicker } from 'datespan'

/** Full control with the hook: your own markup, styled with Tailwind on `data-*` attributes. */
export function MonthRange() {
  const picker = useMonthRangePicker({ presets: [lastNMonths(6)], onChange: (v) => console.log(v?.from, v?.to) })

  return (
    <div className="flex gap-4">
      {picker.presets.map((p) => (
        <button key={p.key} {...p.getProps({ className: 'data-[active]:font-bold' })}>
          {p.label}
        </button>
      ))}
      {picker.grids.map((g) => (
        <div key={g.part}>
          <button {...g.getPrevProps()}>‹</button>
          <span {...g.getTitleProps()}>{g.title}</span>
          <button {...g.getNextProps()}>›</button>
          <div {...g.getGridProps({ className: 'grid gap-1' })}>
            {g.rows.map((row, i) => (
              <div key={i} {...g.getRowProps({ className: 'grid grid-cols-3 gap-1' })}>
                {row.map((m) => (
                  <div
                    key={m.key}
                    {...m.getProps({
                      className:
                        'rounded py-2 text-center data-[in-range]:bg-blue-100 data-[preview]:bg-blue-50 data-[selected]:bg-blue-600 data-[selected]:text-white data-[disabled]:text-gray-300',
                    })}
                  >
                    {m.label}
                  </div>
                ))}
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}
```
<!-- /example -->

<!-- example: date-hook -->
```tsx
import { useDatePicker } from 'datespan'

/** Full control with the hook. The same markup serves the day, month and year views. */
export function Calendar() {
  const dp = useDatePicker({ onChange: (d) => console.log(d) })

  return (
    <div>
      <button {...dp.getPrevProps()}>‹</button>
      <button {...dp.getTitleProps()}>{dp.title}</button>
      <button {...dp.getNextProps()}>›</button>
      <div {...dp.getGridProps()}>
        {dp.weekdays.length > 0 && (
          <div {...dp.getRowProps()}>
            {dp.weekdays.map((w) => (
              <div key={w.day} {...w.getProps()}>
                {w.label}
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}
        {dp.rows.map((row, i) => (
          <div key={i} {...dp.getRowProps()}>
            {row.map((c) => (
              <div key={c.key} {...c.getProps()}>
                {c.label}
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```
<!-- /example -->

Every getter accepts your own props and merges them:
- Event handlers run yours first. Call `e.preventDefault()` to skip ours.
- `className`s are joined.
- `style`s and refs are merged.

## Styling

Each cell's state is mirrored as `data-*` attributes, present only when true:
- **Every cell:** `data-selected`, `data-disabled`, `data-today`.
- **Date cells** also get `data-outside`.
- **Month range cells** also get `data-in-range`, `data-range-start`, `data-range-end` and `data-preview` (the hovered range).
- **Preset buttons** get `data-active`.

The compound components render this markup:
- `<div data-datespan-grid>` (with `data-part="from|to"` for month range grids)
- inside it, `<div data-datespan-header>` (‹ title ›), then the `role="grid"` / `role="row"` / `role="gridcell"` elements

Pass `className` (or any prop) to `Grids`, `Calendar` or `Presets` to add your own.

```css
[role='gridcell'][data-in-range] { background: #e3ebff; }
[role='gridcell'][data-selected] { background: #2456d8; color: white; }
[role='gridcell'][data-disabled] { color: #a7aeb8; }
[data-datespan-header] { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; }
[role='row'] { display: flex; } [role='gridcell'] { flex: 1; text-align: center; }

/* usePopover doesn't position anything: anchor the popup to the trigger's wrapper */
.wrapper { position: relative; }
.popup { position: absolute; top: calc(100% + 4px); left: 0; z-index: 10; }
```

## API

### `useMonthRangePicker(options)` / `<MonthRangePicker.Root {...options}>`

| Option | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | | `{ start: Date, end: Date } \| null` |
| `onChange` | | `(v: { start, end, from, to, preset? } \| null) => void` |
| `layout` | `'dual'` | `'stepped'` = one grid, first month then last |
| `commit` | `'instant'` | `'confirm'` = keep a draft until Apply |
| `min` / `max` | | month precision; `max: new Date()` forbids the future |
| `isMonthDisabled` | | `(month: Date) => boolean` |
| `maxSpan` | | max months in a range |
| `presets` | `[]` | `lastNMonths(n)` (ends today), `lastNDays(n)`, `calendarYear(-1, { label: 'Last year' })` (default label is the year number, e.g. `2024`), `yearToDate()`, or `{ key, label, range: (today) => ({ start, end }) }` |
| `columns` | `3` | months per row |
| `open` | | pass `pop.isOpen`: closing the popover discards an unapplied draft |
| `locale` / `labels` / `today` | | localization, translations, fixed "today" for tests |

It returns:
- `value` (with `from`/`to`, including for the initial value), `draft` and `label` (text for a trigger button)
- `grids` (each with `title` and `rows`) and `presets`
- `step` and `setStep` (stepped layout)
- `cancel`, `clear`, `getApplyProps` and `getCancelProps`

The compound parts are `Presets`, `Grids`, `Apply` and `Cancel`.

### `useDatePicker(options)` / `<DatePicker.Root {...options}>`

| Option | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` / `defaultValue` | | `Date \| null` |
| `onChange` | | `(d: Date \| null) => void`, local midnight |
| `min` / `max` / `isDateDisabled` | | |
| `format` | `'yyyy-MM-dd'` | input pattern from `yyyy MM M dd d` |
| `weekStartsOn` | locale | `0` = Sunday |
| `fixedWeeks` | `false` | always 6 rows |
| `defaultMonth` | value or today | |
| `locale` / `labels` / `today` | | |

It returns:
- `value`, `title`, `view` and `setView`
- `month` and `goTo`
- `weekdays` and `rows`
- `isInputInvalid`, for showing an error message
- the getters: `getGridProps`, `getRowProps`, `getTitleProps`, `getPrevProps`, `getNextProps` and `getInputProps`

The compound parts are `Input` and `Calendar`.

### `usePopover(options?)`

`{ open?, defaultOpen?, onOpenChange? }` → `isOpen`, `open`, `close`, `toggle`, `getTriggerProps`, `getPopoverProps`.
- It handles Escape, outside click and focus leaving the popup.
- It moves focus to the picker on open, and back to the trigger on close.
- It does **not** position the popup. Use CSS, the native `popover` attribute, or Floating UI.

## Keyboard

| Key | Day grid | Month/year grid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | move one cell (one week for ↑/↓) | move one cell (one row for ↑/↓) |
| Home / End | start / end of the week | start / end of the row |
| PageUp / PageDown | one month | one year |
| Shift+PageUp / PageDown | one year | one year |
| Enter / Space | select | select |
| Escape (in the popover) | close | close |

## For AI coding agents

- **[`llms-full.txt`](./llms-full.txt):** this README plus every type, with JSDoc, in one file. It also ships in the package at `node_modules/datespan/llms-full.txt`.
- **`npx datespan agents`:** installs a skill for Claude Code, a rule for Cursor and a section in `AGENTS.md`.

## Notes

- **`'use client'`:** the build starts with `'use client'` for React Server Components. Vite may log a harmless `MODULE_LEVEL_DIRECTIVE` warning about it.
- **Typed input:** `DatePicker` `onChange` also fires when typed text is committed (on blur or Enter).

# Type reference (dist/index.d.ts)

```ts
import { AllHTMLAttributes, ReactNode, Ref } from "react";
/** HTML attributes plus `data-*` and `ref`: what prop getters accept and return. */
type Props = Omit<AllHTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, 'type'> & {
  type?: any;
  ref?: Ref<any>;
  [data: `data-${string}`]: unknown;
};
/** A prop getter: pass your own props to merge them. */
type Getter = (props?: Props) => Props;
/** A day, month or year in a grid. Every `is*` flag is mirrored as a `data-*` attribute. */
interface Cell {
  /** Local midnight at the start of the day/month/year. */
  date: Date;
  /** `'2025-08-05'`, `'2025-08'` or `'2025'`, handy as a React key. */
  key: string;
  /** Localized text to show: `'5'`, `'Aug'`, `'2025'`. */
  label: string;
  isSelected: boolean;
  isDisabled: boolean;
  /** Contains today. */
  isToday: boolean;
  /** Day view: belongs to the previous/next month. */
  isOutside?: boolean;
  /** Month range: inside the range, endpoints included. */
  isInRange?: boolean;
  isRangeStart?: boolean;
  isRangeEnd?: boolean;
  /** Month range: inside the range being hovered towards in the "to" grid. */
  isPreview?: boolean;
  /** Props for the cell element (`div`/`td`, not `button`): ARIA, `data-*` state, click and keyboard handling. */
  getProps: Getter;
}
export type DatePickerView = 'day' | 'month' | 'year';
declare const LABELS$1: {
  prevYear: string;
  nextYear: string;
  prevMonth: string;
  nextMonth: string;
  prevYears: string;
  nextYears: string;
};
export interface UseDatePickerOptions {
  /** Controlled value. `null` = empty. Leave `undefined` for uncontrolled. */
  value?: Date | null;
  /** Initial value when uncontrolled. */
  defaultValue?: Date | null;
  /** Fires with local midnight of the picked day, or `null` when the input is cleared. */
  onChange?: (date: Date | null) => void;
  /** Earliest selectable day. */
  min?: Date;
  /** Latest selectable day. */
  max?: Date;
  isDateDisabled?: (date: Date) => boolean;
  /** BCP 47 locale for month/weekday names. Defaults to the browser locale. */
  locale?: string;
  /** 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Defaults to the locale's convention when the browser knows it, else Sunday. */
  weekStartsOn?: number;
  /** Always render 6 weeks so the grid height never jumps. */
  fixedWeeks?: boolean;
  /** Initial visible month (any date inside it). Defaults to the value's month, else today's. */
  defaultMonth?: Date;
  /** Numeric pattern for `getInputProps()` using `yyyy`, `MM`, `M`, `dd`, `d`. Default `'yyyy-MM-dd'`. */
  format?: string;
  /** Override "today" (tests, SSR, server time). */
  today?: Date;
  /** Translations: `{ prevMonth, nextMonth, prevYear, nextYear, prevYears, nextYears }`. */
  labels?: Partial<typeof LABELS$1>;
}
export interface Weekday {
  /** Short name, e.g. `'Mon'` (the long name is its `aria-label`). */
  label: string;
  /** 0 = Sunday. */
  day: number;
  getProps: Getter;
}
export interface DatePickerApi {
  value: Date | null;
  /** `'day'`, or zoomed out to `'month'` / `'year'` by clicking the title. */
  view: DatePickerView;
  setView: (view: DatePickerView) => void;
  /** 1st of the visible month. */
  month: Date;
  goTo: (date: Date) => void;
  /** "October 2026" (day view), "2026" (month view), "2016 – 2027" (year view). */
  title: string;
  /** Column headers. Only filled in the day view. */
  weekdays: Weekday[];
  /** The current view's cells: weeks of days, or 4 rows of 3 months / years. */
  rows: Cell[][];
  getGridProps: Getter;
  getRowProps: Getter;
  /** Button showing `title`: labels the grid, announces navigation, click zooms out (day → month → year → day). */
  getTitleProps: Getter;
  getPrevProps: Getter;
  getNextProps: Getter;
  /**
   * Text input that parses `format` on blur/Enter (firing `onChange`) and follows typing in the calendar.
   * Sets `aria-invalid`; add `aria-describedby` for your error message.
   */
  getInputProps: Getter;
  /** The typed text is not a valid, selectable date (show an error message). */
  isInputInvalid: boolean;
}
/**
 * Headless single-date picker: a day grid with month/year zoom views, an optional parsing
 * text input, min/max/disabled dates, locale-aware week start and full keyboard support
 * (arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, Shift+PageUp/PageDown, Enter/Space).
 * For less code use `<DatePicker.Root>`.
 */
export declare function useDatePicker(o?: UseDatePickerOptions): DatePickerApi;
interface GridViewProps extends Props {
  /** Cell content. Default: `cell.label`. */
  renderCell?: (cell: Cell) => ReactNode;
}
/**
 * Unstyled compound components over `useDatePicker`. `Root` takes the hook's options and
 * accepts a render function `(picker) => …`; `DatePicker.useContext()` returns the picker.
 *
 * @example
 * <DatePicker.Root value={date} onChange={setDate}>
 *   <DatePicker.Input aria-label="Date of birth" />
 *   <DatePicker.Calendar />
 * </DatePicker.Root>
 */
export declare const DatePicker: {
  Root: ({ children, ...options }: UseDatePickerOptions & {
    children?: import("react").ReactNode | ((api: DatePickerApi) => import("react").ReactNode);
  }) => import("react").JSX.Element;
  useContext: () => DatePickerApi;
} & {
  /** Header (‹ title ›; the title zooms out to months/years) and the grid for the current view. */
  Calendar: (props: GridViewProps) => import("react").JSX.Element;
  Input: (props: Props) => import("react").JSX.Element;
};
/** An inclusive range of local `Date`s. */
export interface DateRange {
  start: Date;
  end: Date;
}
/**
 * A named shortcut such as "Last 12 months". `range` receives "today" so presets stay
 * correct across midnight and are deterministic in tests.
 */
export interface Preset {
  /** Stable id, reported back as `onChange(value).preset`. */
  key: string;
  /** Text shown on the preset button and on the trigger when the preset is active. */
  label: string | ((today: Date) => string);
  range: (today: Date) => DateRange;
}
interface PresetOptions {
  key?: string;
  label?: string;
}
/**
 * The last `n` months, ending today. The first month starts on its 1st.
 * Pass `includeCurrent: false` for the last `n` *complete* months.
 * @example lastNMonths(12) // Nov 1 last year → today
 */
export declare const lastNMonths: (n: number, { key, label, includeCurrent }?: PresetOptions & {
  includeCurrent?: boolean;
}) => Preset;
/**
 * The last `n` days including today.
 * @example lastNDays(30)
 */
export declare const lastNDays: (n: number, { key, label }?: PresetOptions) => Preset;
/**
 * A whole calendar year relative to today: `0` = this year, `-1` = last year.
 * The default label is the year number, e.g. `'2025'`.
 */
export declare const calendarYear: (offset?: number, { key, label }?: PresetOptions) => Preset;
/** January 1st of this year → today. */
export declare const yearToDate: ({ key, label }?: PresetOptions) => Preset;
export type MonthRangePart = 'from' | 'to';
/** What `onChange` receives: the range plus ready-to-use ISO months and the matched preset. */
export interface MonthRangeValue extends DateRange {
  /** First month, `'2025-08'`. */
  from: string;
  /** Last month, `'2025-10'`. */
  to: string;
  /** Key of the preset this range matches, if any. */
  preset?: string;
}
declare const LABELS: {
  prevYear: string;
  nextYear: string;
  from: string;
  to: string;
};
export interface UseMonthRangePickerOptions {
  /** Controlled value. `null` = nothing selected. Leave `undefined` for uncontrolled. */
  value?: DateRange | null;
  /** Initial value when uncontrolled. */
  defaultValue?: DateRange | null;
  /**
   * Fires with a complete range (`start` = 1st of the first month 00:00, `end` = last ms of the
   * last month), or `null` after `clear()`. With `commit: 'confirm'` it fires on Apply only.
   */
  onChange?: (value: MonthRangeValue | null) => void;
  /**
   * `'dual'` (default): a "from" grid and a "to" grid side by side.
   * `'stepped'`: one grid; pick the first month, then the last (mobile friendly).
   * Switching layout keeps the selection, so you can drive it from a media query.
   */
  layout?: 'dual' | 'stepped';
  /** `'instant'` (default): `onChange` on every complete selection. `'confirm'`: keep a draft until Apply. */
  commit?: 'instant' | 'confirm';
  /** Earliest selectable month (any date inside it). */
  min?: Date;
  /** Latest selectable month (any date inside it), e.g. `new Date()` to forbid the future. */
  max?: Date;
  /** Disable individual months. Receives the 1st of the month. */
  isMonthDisabled?: (month: Date) => boolean;
  /** Maximum number of months in a range (inclusive). */
  maxSpan?: number;
  /** Shortcuts, see `lastNMonths`, `lastNDays`, `calendarYear`, `yearToDate`. */
  presets?: Preset[];
  /** Months per row (default 3). Drives ArrowUp/ArrowDown. */
  columns?: number;
  /** BCP 47 locale for month names and years. Defaults to the browser locale. */
  locale?: string;
  /** Override "today" (tests, SSR, server time). */
  today?: Date;
  /** Translations: `{ from, to, prevYear, nextYear }`. */
  labels?: Partial<typeof LABELS>;
  /**
   * Whether the popover holding the picker is open (`pop.isOpen`). Closing it any way
   * (Escape, outside click, Cancel) discards an unapplied draft.
   */
  open?: boolean;
}
export interface MonthGrid {
  part: MonthRangePart;
  /** "From" / "To". */
  label: string;
  year: number;
  /** "From 2025": labels the grid; render it with `getTitleProps()`. */
  title: string;
  /** Rows of `columns` months; render each with `getRowProps()` for a valid ARIA grid. */
  rows: Cell[][];
  getGridProps: Getter;
  getRowProps: Getter;
  getTitleProps: Getter;
  getPrevProps: Getter;
  getNextProps: Getter;
}
export interface PresetItem {
  key: string;
  label: string;
  isActive: boolean;
  /** Button props: `aria-pressed`, `data-active`, click selects the preset. */
  getProps: Getter;
}
export interface MonthRangePickerApi {
  /** The committed value, with `from`/`to` ISO months, e.g. to show or send the initial range. */
  value: MonthRangeValue | null;
  /** The in-progress selection (equals `value` unless `commit: 'confirm'` or mid-selection). */
  draft: {
    start: Date | null;
    end: Date | null;
  };
  /** Which half is being picked. Only the stepped layout shows it. */
  step: MonthRangePart;
  setStep: (step: MonthRangePart) => void;
  /** Two grids for `'dual'`, one for `'stepped'`. */
  grids: MonthGrid[];
  presets: PresetItem[];
  /** Text for a trigger button: the active preset's label, or e.g. "Aug – Oct 2025". Empty when no value. */
  label: string;
  /** Drop the draft and return to the committed value. */
  cancel: () => void;
  clear: () => void;
  /** Commits the draft (confirm mode); disabled while the draft is incomplete. */
  getApplyProps: Getter;
  /** Calls `cancel()`. Merge your own `onClick` to also close a popover. */
  getCancelProps: Getter;
}
/**
 * Formats a range at month precision: "Aug – Oct 2025", "Nov 2024 – Feb 2025", or "Aug 2025".
 */
export declare const formatMonthRange: (range: DateRange, locale?: string) => string;
/**
 * Headless month range picker: "from" and "to" month grids (or one stepped grid), presets,
 * draft/confirm flow, constraints and full keyboard support. Renders nothing; spread the
 * returned prop getters onto your own elements and style them with `data-*` attributes.
 * For less code use `<MonthRangePicker.Root>`.
 */
export declare function useMonthRangePicker(o?: UseMonthRangePickerOptions): MonthRangePickerApi;
/**
 * Unstyled compound components over `useMonthRangePicker`. `Root` takes the hook's options and
 * accepts a render function `(picker) => …`; `MonthRangePicker.useContext()` returns the picker.
 *
 * @example
 * <MonthRangePicker.Root presets={[lastNMonths(12)]} onChange={setRange}>
 *   <MonthRangePicker.Presets aria-label="Presets" />
 *   <MonthRangePicker.Grids />
 * </MonthRangePicker.Root>
 */
export declare const MonthRangePicker: {
  Root: ({ children, ...options }: UseMonthRangePickerOptions & {
    children?: import("react").ReactNode | ((api: MonthRangePickerApi) => import("react").ReactNode);
  }) => import("react").JSX.Element;
  useContext: () => MonthRangePickerApi;
} & {
  /** Preset buttons in a `role="group"`; the active one has `aria-pressed` and `data-active`. */
  Presets: (props: Props) => import("react").JSX.Element;
  /** Every grid of the current layout: "From" and "To" for `'dual'`, one for `'stepped'`. */
  Grids: (props: GridViewProps) => import("react").JSX.Element;
  Apply: (props: Props) => import("react").JSX.Element;
  Cancel: (props: Props) => import("react").JSX.Element;
};
export interface UsePopoverOptions {
  /** Controlled open state. */
  open?: boolean;
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
}
export interface Popover {
  isOpen: boolean;
  open: () => void;
  /** Closes and returns focus to the trigger. Does nothing when already closed. */
  close: () => void;
  toggle: () => void;
  getTriggerProps: Getter;
  /** Spread on the popup. Render it only while `isOpen`. */
  getPopoverProps: Getter;
}
/**
 * Open/close behaviour for a picker popup, without positioning: ARIA wiring, Escape,
 * outside click, focus-out, focus into the grid on open and back to the trigger on close.
 * Position the popup yourself (CSS, the native `popover` attribute, or Floating UI).
 *
 * @example
 * const pop = usePopover()
 * const picker = useDatePicker({ value, onChange: (d) => { setValue(d); pop.close() } })
 * <button {...pop.getTriggerProps()}>Pick a date</button>
 * {pop.isOpen && <div {...pop.getPopoverProps({ className: 'popup' })}>…</div>}
 */
export declare function usePopover(o?: UsePopoverOptions): Popover;
/**
 * Formats a date with numeric tokens: `yyyy`, `MM`, `M`, `dd`, `d`.
 * @example formatDate(new Date(2025, 7, 5), 'dd/MM/yyyy') // '05/08/2025'
 */
export declare const formatDate: (d: Date, pattern: string) => string;
/**
 * Parses a string written in a numeric `pattern` (see {@link formatDate}).
 * Returns `null` for malformed input or impossible dates like 31/02/2025.
 * @example parseDate('05/08/2025', 'dd/MM/yyyy') // Date(2025, 7, 5)
 */
export declare const parseDate: (s: string, pattern: string) => Date | null;
export type { Cell, Getter, Props };
```
